comparator.sourceNotes: The broad Linguistics route closes 60+60+60. Language X is instantiated as Czech 1-4, the first complete documented eligible sequence after an empty Catalan allocation, with sequential prerequisites and English instruction. Czech is not added as an instruction language. Specialization Linguistics remains one 6-EC unit rather than invented formal tracks; 30 EC of genuine profiling remains open. Academic Literacy Test and recurring tutoring are zero-credit formation.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Speech sounds, word formation, grammar, semantics, pragmatics and cross-linguistic structure
Language acquisition, psycholinguistics, cognition, development, neurolinguistics and clinical language study
Language variation, sociolinguistics, multilingualism, interaction and communication in society
Experimental and field research, statistics, language documentation and independent linguistic inquiry
adjacent: Written, spoken and multimodal discourse, rhetoric, literary interpretation and media communication
Speech processing, language data and computational language applications
questions: How do mind, society and media shape language use and meaning?

alternatives.label: Language, cognition & communication research
alternatives.concept: Study language through psycholinguistics, cognitive science, developmental and social psychology, stylistics, rhetoric, experimental methods, data science and computational analysis. This is the strongest related-fields response, not a substitute for the comparator’s formal linguistics, phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, fieldwork and clinical-linguistics sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines psycholinguistics and cognition with experimental research, statistics, data science, programming, algorithms, rhetoric and textual meaning. The label describes that related-fields centre and avoids claiming a full Linguistics programme.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and eight level-300 courses. Every course is offered in its assigned Fall-2026-start term. Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Perception & Action, Higher Order Functions, Psycholinguistics, Lifespan Developmental Psychology and the Advanced Research Seminar; Introduction to Programming precedes Algorithms & Data Structures. Introductory research, data, rhetoric, stylistics, sociology and literary study precede the advanced empirical, computational and interpretive work.

alternatives.label: Language, discourse & media in society
alternatives.concept: Study language as social and cultural practice through stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, modern-language learning, sociology, literature, film and media. The route concentrates on discourse, identity, multilingual communication and mediated meaning while preserving formal linguistic structure and language-science methods as explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route concentrates on social language use, rhetoric, stylistics, psycholinguistics, literature and media. Its label states discourse and media as the organising fields rather than presenting it as formal Linguistics.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and eight level-300 courses. Every course is offered in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics by four semesters. Introductory sociology, literature, rhetoric, Dutch, stylistics and film/media precede advanced social theory, persuasion, adaptation, media analysis, literary meaning and documentary work.
alternatives.distinctness: Thirteen courses / 97.5 EC differ in each direction. The cognition-and-research route uses neuroscience, philosophy of mind, experimental and quantitative methods, developmental and social psychology, programming, algorithms and data science. The discourse-and-media route instead develops a modern language, modern sociology, wider literature and a five-course film/media sequence. The change follows distinct evidenced interests in experimental language/mind research and in language as social, cultural and mediated practice.

candidates.label: Language, discourse and media in society
Formal linguistic structure and cross-linguistic comparison

selection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes are defensible. The closest response combines psycholinguistics, cognition, developmental and social psychology, experimental methods, data science, programming, algorithms, rhetoric and textual meaning. The second concentrates on discourse, social language use, modern-language learning, literature, film and media. They differ by thirteen courses / 97.5 EC. A formal-structure and cross-linguistic programme is not feasible because UCR lacks the required sequence in phonetics, transcription, phonology, morphology, syntax, typology, field linguistics and language documentation; a language-technology route would likewise rely on generic computing courses without dedicated speech or natural-language processing content.

Both analyse how linguistic form creates meaning; UCR provides stylistics and literary linguistics rather than a full semantics-and-pragmatics course.
Both involve beginning modern-language acquisition; UCR teaches Dutch and provides one course rather than the comparator’s four-course Czech sequence.
UCR has no introductory linguistics survey covering the comparator’s formal subfields and scientific methods.

UCR has no transcription course or practical phonetic-transcription sequence.

UCR has no cumulative linguistic-theory course following formal linguistics prerequisites.
Both concern the neural basis of cognition; UCR provides general neurobiology rather than a dedicated neurolinguistics course.
Both directly study psycholinguistics, including production, comprehension, acquisition, bilingualism, semantics and language-thought relations.
Both address language acquisition in human development; UCR embeds it within lifespan developmental psychology rather than a dedicated first-language-acquisition course.
Both examine cognition and mental representation; UCR is a general Philosophy of Mind course rather than a language-and-cognition humanities seminar.
UCR Psycholinguistics discusses acquisition and bilingualism but does not reproduce a dedicated second-language-acquisition course.
UCR has no clinical-linguistics course or clinical language assessment practice.
Research methods, data and language technology
Both develop research design and empirical inquiry; UCR provides a general methods-and-statistics foundation rather than a linguistics-specific first-year project.
Both develop experimental design and statistical analysis; UCR teaches these in psychology rather than as linguistics-specific methods.
UCR offers general data science, machine learning and algorithms but no dedicated speech-processing course.
UCR has no formal Linguistics specialization module or field-linguistics equivalent.
The genuine 30-EC profiling space remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.
The compulsory Linguistics thesis remains separate; UCR optional independent research is comparison-only and not scheduled degree credit.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives study psycholinguistics, cognition, development, research methods, data science, rhetoric, stylistics, social language use, literature and media. UCR does not offer the comparator’s cumulative sequence in phonetics, transcription, phonology, morphology, syntax, typology, field linguistics, language documentation, clinical linguistics or speech processing. These are therefore related cognitive, communication and cultural routes rather than Linguistics equivalents.
